executive_summary: Your supply chain has crystallized into two distinct crisis zones, both AMBER-worthy. The first is geopolitical concentration: five suppliers across printing substrates and nicotine (Stora Enso, IP Sun, Sappi, ITC, Porton) sit on active conflict peripheries or in US-China friction points, creating correlated risk if tensions escalate. The second is immediate market stress with unknown triggers: Jabil (mechanical), Infineon (EE components), and Texas Instruments have suffered unexplained stock drops of 4–5%, and Jabil's CRITICAL risk level warrants urgent clarification—this could signal debt distress, capacity issues, or external shocks not yet public. AMCOR and the two critical-exposure EMS players in China (Huizhou BYD, Smoore) add supply concentration risk on top of geopolitical exposure. Act on Jabil and Infineon immediately (call investor relations, check supply continuity); then map dual sourcing options for geopolitical clusters, starting with nicotine (ITC/Porton) and EMS (China bases). The EU macro data is current but US and China indicators are stale—prioritize refreshing those before escalation.
